Evidence: A awwal, adj. First, prior, foremost; Perder p. 92 explicitly states that awal first is borrowed from an Arabic-derived word found in both Urdu and Pashto, rather than formed with productive ordinal -m. Record the established loan origin while retaining Urdu versus Pashto as unresolved immediate alternatives. The local donor inventory has no resolved corresponding Urdu or Pashto node. Do not derive this suppletive ordinal from Dameli one, attach directly to Arabic without transmission evidence, or conflate it with avaluka/avaluki old.

Evidence: P āsmān, vulg. asmān, s.m. Sky, firmament; Dameli āsmān sky matches Persian āsmān and the same survey’s Khowar and Gawarbati sky words. The Persian form and meaning are independently documented by Tafażżolī’s Āsmān article and the existing Persian node f_lmwk7knn4svus. These support a probable Persian-origin regional loan; they do not identify whether Dameli received it directly from Persian or through a neighbouring language. No edge to the available Persian node is proposed merely because it exists.

Evidence: P yād, s.f. Remembrance, recollection; memory; Perder example 7 glosses yat remembrance in names are remembered. Platts Persian yād has remembrance and yād honā be remembered. The Pashto plural on adjacent nam-una is contact context, not proof that yat itself was borrowed directly from Pashto.
